finer.rule: 19200 cells are run if between the two finest grids the speed moved by more than 0.1 % of CJ, the pressure at the sonic point by more than 1 % or the highest pressure by more than 2 % (or one of them holds no detonation), and the run is expected to stay below 15 minutes

pass_rules: Required by the problem: wave speed within 2 % of 1978.54 m/s, on the finest grid; every grid is reported.
Required by the problem: from 10 microseconds on the burning front within 1 mm of the pressure front, on every grid.
The run does not break: no value that is not a number, every cell's chemistry status 0.
Total mass and atoms of each element kept within 1e-9; total energy within 1e-9 (the solver stores it, so only the guard can change it).
expected: 0.1 mm cells: speed within 1 % of CJ (OpenFOAM's trial: 1.1 % below); highest pressure 2.0 to 2.6 MPa (trial 1.97; a resolved front has 2.81).

Finer grids: the highest pressure rises towards 2.81 MPa. On the finest grids the front may pulse (a resolved one-dimensional detonation in this mixture is known to be unstable), so the highest pressure may swing above 2.81 MPa; the speed over the second half stays within 1 % of CJ.
Gap 0 to 0.3 mm on every grid.

Burnt state at the sonic point: pressure within 5 % and temperature within 3 % of CJ (1.581 MPa, 2970 K). Read 2 to 6 mm behind the front: 1.4 to 1.6 MPa, because the gas behind a detonation in a closed tube expands at once.
The three orders of splitting differ by less than 0.2 % in speed; flow then chemistry stays the default because it is the cheapest.
The guard is not used with van Leer.
Cost in one dimension: the GPU is idle, a step costs 0.3 to 0.6 ms whatever the grid; 1200 cells take about 2 s (trial: 689 s).
Cost on the stacked tube: flow 15 to 30 ns per cell and step; chemistry 30 to 60 ns with bs23 (more than half of the time) and 8 to 20 ns with the chosen setting.
